A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T* research work. All eight pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.2, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SDAR training and mathematical-reasoning evaluations, including accuracy results, training trajectories, decoding-order measurements, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports tokens-per-forward measurements in Table 1.

M1.justification: The stated update schedule is revised: v1 describes unshifted updates on the first half of an epoch and shifted updates on the second half; v3 pairs both within K_B iterations before block expansion. Algorithm 1 adds the corresponding inner loop. TRACERL, the B/2 shift, and block doubling remain; actual implementation changes are not independently established.

E1.justification: Both versions use 8K level-3–5 Openr1math training problems and evaluate mathematical reasoning on MATH500, GSM8K, and AIME24. The added efficiency measurements concern retained decoding scenarios, without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the original SDAR checkpoints and direct TRACERL baselines. Table 1 also retains Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen2.5-1.5B; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: v3 adds tokens per forward (TPF) as an efficiency metric. Section 2.2 also replaces the stated one-epoch stage budget with an unspecified K_B update budget. Model sizes, sampling settings, Pass@3 evaluation, and best-MATH500 checkpoint selection remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 adds an analysis of whether larger blocks increase tokens finalized per forward pass and whether RL preserves that benefit. Existing training-collapse analysis, LocalStrict analysis, and Appendix A.2 case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added TPF results introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds TPF results: T* reports 2.95, 3.38, and 3.80 at block sizes 8, 16, and 32, respectively, versus base-model values of 2.91, 3.38, and 3.74. Existing accuracy and LocalStrict entries, Appendix Table 2 scores, and case-study outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their substantive mathematical content remain unchanged. v3 explains the existing corruption process, confidence threshold, and token-action notation more explicitly, without adding a theoretical result, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that progressive block scaling preserves reasoning performance while enabling greater decoding parallelism and can induce a noncanonical schedule. The abstract's slight modal rewording does not materially alter these contributions; TPF supplies new support for the retained efficiency motivation.

C2.justification: v3 interprets similar TPF after RL as preserving parallelism and potentially improving throughput or latency when forward passes dominate. It removes Section 2.2's explicit rationale that shifting reduces boundary artifacts and helps positional adaptation. The collapse explanation and stated limitations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 explicitly exposes K_B as the per-stage update-count parameter, and Section 2.1 clarifies position-token actions. No numerical K_B is supplied. Hardware, optimizer, learning rate, rollout sampling counts, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the dependence on TRACERL and the positioning of internal schedule learning as complementary to external tree/graph search.

P1.justification: v3 expands the title's acronyms, corrects affiliation spellings, expands explanations around existing equations and actions, and rewrites Section 2.2. These are localized revisions; the overall section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a TPF column and revised caption. Algorithm 1 is expanded and relocated from page 2 to page 4, Figure 3 switches columns, and Figure 2's caption expands. The figure graphics and appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies stage-wise training through the revised algorithm and adds quantitative evidence for decoding parallelism in Table 1, while retaining the original accuracy and appendix evidence. These provide a limited overall gain in clarity and empirical support. Reproducibility remains incomplete because K_B is unspecified, and TPF supports efficiency only as a proxy, without measured wall-clock gains.
